title: The senses
subtitle: look tired, sound like an alarm, feel as if
summary: Talk about what you see, hear, taste, smell and feel, and tell apart pairs like look and watch or hear and listen.

lesson.heading: The five basic senses
rows: the ability to know if food is sweet, salty, and so on
the ability to know from the air that bread is fresh
the ability to feel something with your hand or skin

lesson.heading: Sense verb + adjective
lesson.text: We use the sense verbs with an adjective to say what our eyes, ears, mouth, nose or hands tell us.

examples.note: = from another country, from what I could hear
damp = slightly wet, often in an unpleasant way

lesson.note: These verbs are also nouns: I like the look of this hotel. I love the sound of his voice.

lesson.heading: Sense verb + like + noun
lesson.text: Use **like** + a noun to say that two things are similar. You cannot use *like* before an adjective.

examples.text: Have you ever had a nectarine? They **look like** peaches.
Did you hear that noise? It **sounded like** an alarm.

examples.note: You can also say smells of coconut.

examples.text: Don't you think this material **feels like** silk?

lesson.heading: Sense verb + as if / as though + clause
lesson.text: Use **as if** or **as though** and then a whole clause (subject + verb) to describe what you think is happening.

examples.text: That boy **looks as if** he's trying to get over the wall.
It **sounded as though** they had a good time on holiday.
Put your hand on the radiator. Does it **feel as if** it's getting warm?
Have you tried the soup? It **tastes as if** it needs a bit more salt.

lesson.heading: seem and appear
lesson.text: We also use **seem** and **appear** to describe a feeling about someone or something after we have seen them or talked to them. Before *like* + noun, we usually use **seem**.

examples.text: I saw Will and he **seemed** quite happy.
The shop **appears** to be very busy.
Amelia wants to travel a bit, which **seems like** a good idea.
Alina didn't ask any questions. She **seemed as though** she wasn't interested.

left.label: see = you are able to see
left.text: **See** is about your eyes working; **watch** means pay attention to something for a long time.
examples: If you look at the map, you can **see** the church on the left.
I **saw** a film at the cinema.
They've been **watching** that man for weeks.

right.label: look = you look carefully
right.text: **Look (at)** means turn your eyes to something on purpose. It can also mean pay attention.
examples: Quick. Come and **look at** this man walking by.
He ran into me because he wasn't **looking**.
If you **look** carefully, you can see how the trick is done.

lesson.heading: hear and listen; touch and feel

left.label: hear / touch
left.text: **Hear** = your ears work. **Touch** = put your hand on something.
examples: I **heard** what she said, but I wasn't listening.
She turned up the volume but I still couldn't **hear** it.

right.label: listen / feel
right.text: **Listen (to)** = pay attention with your ears. **Feel** = put your hand on something to discover what it is like.
examples: I was **listening to** the radio when I heard a terrible noise.
Tom wasn't **listening to** what I was saying.
Just **feel** my feet. Aren't they cold?

lesson.text: We say *I saw a film at the cinema*, but *I watched a film on TV*. You cannot ~~watch a film at the cinema~~.

exercises.prompt: Match each sense with what it means.

pairs.right: the ability to know if food is sweet or salty
the ability to know from the air that bread is fresh
the ability to feel something with your hand

exercises.prompt: I was very angry with Tom - he just wasn't ___ to what I was saying.
exercises.explanation: Listen to = pay attention with your ears. Hear = your ears work.

exercises.prompt: She turned up the volume but I still couldn't ___ it.
exercises.explanation: Hear = be able to hear. We do not say couldn't listen it.

exercises.prompt: There's a good film on at the cinema. Have you ___ it?
exercises.explanation: We see a film at the cinema; we watch a film on TV.

exercises.prompt: Quick. Come and ___ this man walking by.
exercises.explanation: Look at = turn your eyes to something on purpose.

exercises.prompt: We ___ the birds while they were eating food from the bird table.
exercises.explanation: Watch = pay attention to something for some time.

exercises.prompt: You mustn't ___ the paintings in the museum.
exercises.explanation: Touch = put your hand on something.

exercises.prompt: Abigail has just taken the cakes out of the oven and they ___.
The sheets on her bed looked expensive, and when I touched them, they ___.
exercises.explanation: Sense verb + like + noun says that two things are similar.

exercises.prompt: I could see something quite tall in the distance. It ___.
exercises.explanation: Look like + noun = it has the appearance of that thing.

exercises.prompt: When I heard the noise I jumped out of bed because it ___.
exercises.explanation: Sound like + noun describes what a noise is similar to.

exercises.statement: I've just met my new class. They look like nice.
exercises.explanation: They seem very nice. / They look nice. We cannot use like before an adjective.

exercises.prompt: Alexei said that Lola was doing well. Put your reply in order.
exercises.answer: It sounds as if she'll pass the exam.
exercises.explanation: Sense verb + as if / as though + clause.
